newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Monkey King shareholders approve restructure plans.
newsitem.headline: Monkey King shareholders approve restructure plans.

text.p: Hubei Monkey King Co Ltd said on Tuesday that shareholders had approved its plan to offer B shares and restructure the company, a major welding materials producer.
The firm would buy 11 welding materials subsidiaries from its parent firm, Monkey King Group, it said in a statement published in Tuesday's Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
It also planned to sell its three subsidiaries, including Monkey King Construction Co, to its parent, it said.
Monkey King Co said it aimed to reduce competition among group companies and through the deal to focus on the welding materials business. No timetable was given for the plan.
It said shareholders also approved a plan to offer B shares, and how the share proceeds would be used. No other details were given.

A spokesman for the listed company told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin that the company planned to issue 100 million B shares by the end of April 1997 and list them in Shenzhen.
He said the company would use the money to build a factory with an annual production capacity of 50,000 tonnes of welding materials.

The company has appointed China Merchants Securities Co as the chief domestic underwriter for the offer, which needs the approval of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the official said. Singapore Development Bank would be the global coordinator.
He said Monkey King Co estimated higher earnings for 1996, but gave no figure. It had net earnings of 41.23 million yuan in 1995 against 52.96 million yuan in 1994.

At the end of June 1996, the company had 252.27 million outstanding shares, comprising 86.82 million state shares, 23.63 million legal person shares, 18.62 million rights shares transferred from state and legal person shareholders, 55,270 staff shares and 123.14 million A shares.
The company's welding materials were being used in the construction of China's multi-billion-yuan Three Gorges Dam project, and it had a 15 percent share of China's domestic market in 1995, he said.
The company would soon begin supplying special welding materials to China's Qinshan Nuclear Power Plant, based in eastern Zhejiang province, he said without elaborating.
